text_blocks.snippet: Ice dams happen in Utah because of rapid temperature swings , sunny winter days, and heat escaping from inside the house into the attic. When snow melts on the warm part of the roof and refreezes on the cold eaves, it creates a ridge of ice that blocks water and leaks into your home.
snippet_highlighted_words: When snow melts on the warm part of the roof and refreezes on the cold eaves, it creates a ridge of ice that blocks water and leaks into your home

text_blocks.snippet: Here is how you can prevent and manage ice dams on your Utah roof.

list.snippet: Use a roof rake: Pull snow off the bottom 3 to 4 feet of your roof edge after heavy storms using a long-handled roof rake. Do this from the ground to stay safe.
Clear gutters: Clean leaves and debris out of gutters in the fall so melting snow can drain freely. Keep gutters and downspouts clear of snow and icicles all winter.

The sock trick (Emergency fix): If an ice dam forms and causes a leak, fill an old sock with calcium chloride or calcium magnesium acetate ice melt. Lay it vertically across the ice dam so it melts a drainage channel for trapped water. Never chip ice with a hammer or sharp tool.

Improve attic insulation: Stop heat from escaping through your ceiling. Ensure your attic has proper insulation depth (8 to 9 inches or more) and seal any air leaks around attic bypasses, light fixtures, and plumbing stacks .
Check attic ventilation: Make sure outside air flows smoothly through your soffit and ridge vents. This keeps the entire roof deck cold so snow doesn't melt unevenly.

Install heat cables or panels: If heat loss cannot be fixed easily, install professional self-regulating de-icing cables or specialized metal edge systems along your eaves and gutters. These create clear paths for water runoff. Local providers like Utah Heat Cable or Any Hour Services can assist with professional setups.
Use steam for removal: If you already have a severe buildup, hire a professional service like Ice Dam Guys that uses low-pressure steam to remove ice safely without damaging your shingles.
